title: Python link/adaptive_sf.py density threshold 10 vs ccp.py 8 — dual-selector divergence
description: Follow-up from b7z9.58 audit: python/src/lichen/link/adaptive_sf.py uses density > 10 (lines :16 pseudocode, :137 explicit step-3) while python/src/lichen/ccp.py adaptive_sf_select uses density > 8 (landed b7z9.30.1 per spec 2a.8 = DENSITY_HIGH 8). Two Python selectors for the same spec procedure with different thresholds — cross-impl parity broken (C gradient.c and Rust rf_health.rs both use 8). Verify which is the canonical selector (ccp.py is the spec-pseudocode oracle per ccp16.json vectors; link/adaptive_sf.py may be the runtime path), then align to 8 and reconcile any tests pinning 10. Related: b7z9.58 (closed cannot-reproduce — current spec says >8 in five places).
